archetypes.name: scan-migration-compat
archetypes.rationale: Three scans migrated from file-presence to reviewer_signals now emit result:skip on old logs, changing counter arithmetic and cumulative delta semantics in audit-compute-counters.sh.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the migration of ns-retry-sidecars, codex-generalist-waste, and trailing-content-no-issues-found to reviewer_signals[] carrier. Focus on: (1) the behavioral change for pre-migration run logs that have no reviewer_signals — these now emit result:skip instead of file-based counts, which changes delta accumulation; verify that cumulative counter arithmetic in audit-compute-counters.sh is correct when mixing skip and fail rows across historical batches. (2) The new NS_RETRIES_SKIPPED_RUNS output key — confirm it is wired into audit report YAML schema, cumulative_counters, and the SKILL.md scan table so operators are not surprised by a new unlabeled counter. (3) Check that the new reviewer-signals scan type in scans-implement.tsv does not cause a registry-drift error for the case arm in audit-scan-run.sh (the case dispatches on name, not type, but verify there is no type-gated dispatch path). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: ns-retry-orphan-dedup
archetypes.rationale: scan_ns_retry_sidecars calls _audit_reviewer_signals_jq twice with different filters; the second call result is used in a jq-based set-membership check that silently degrades if the call fails.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect scan_ns_retry_sidecars in .claude/skills/audit-runs/scripts/audit-scan-run.sh. The function calls _audit_reviewer_signals_jq twice: once to collect ns_retry_reason values, and once to build signaled_bases for orphan dedup. If the second call fails (e.g. malformed JSON in one round-meta.json), signaled_bases is empty or unavailable-string, the jq -e membership check fails silently due to || true, and every legacy sidecar file is counted as an orphan — doubling the count relative to the first-pass signal. Verify whether this double-count path is guarded, and whether the function correctly handles the case where _audit_reviewer_signals_jq's second invocation returns an empty JSON array [] vs a literal unavailable string vs an empty string. Also verify that the legacy-fallback branch (no reviewer_signals at all) correctly emits result:fail with count>0, not result:skip. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: body-severity-extraction
archetypes.rationale: extract_body_severity and extract_focus_area in compose-review-findings.sh operate on the full redacted body before the 2000-char cap but use herestring syntax and awk sub() with the same anchored pattern used elsewhere.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the new extract_body_severity() and extract_focus_area() helpers added to scripts/compose-review-findings.sh and how they are called inside emit_record. Verify: (1) extraction happens from the full $body_redacted before the ${body_redacted:0:2000} truncation — confirm ordering in emit_record. (2) The awk pattern /^[[:space:]-]*\*\*Severity\*\*:[[:space:]]*/ — the character class [[:space:]-]* includes a literal hyphen; confirm this is intentional and does not match unexpected input. (3) The herestring <<<"$1" inside the helper — if $body_redacted contains special shell characters or null bytes that survive redact_field, can the awk invocation fail silently and return empty rather than erroring? (4) When body_severity is empty because the marker is absent, the JSONL emits body_severity:""; verify downstream consumers in fluff-analysis.py handle empty-string vs absent field consistently. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
